text:
Sanjay Rao: @here seeing a sudden burst of 429s from dedicated pools in ap-sg (commitment-az1). Alerts started ~5m ago, admission controller is returning RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/pool-pressure?region=ap-sg :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-442 (priority-high) — paging infra oncall.

Lena Park: Confirming. 80% of requests are landing in queue, median queue_time up from 80ms -> 1.2s, p95 token latency increased. Throughput drop for some customers.

Infra Oncall: Looking at admission logs. It's not a single noisy tenant — multiple tenants hitting commit pool simultaneously after a scheduled job in ap-sg finished. Rate limiter ramped up aggressively and then hit hard cap. Snippet from admission log:
```
2026-03-17T15:03:21Z admit.go:142 ERR admit deny tenant=org-238 reason=rate_limit_exceeded pool=commitment-az1 cap=120 current=124
2026-03-17T15:03:21Z admit.go:143 WARN backpressure queue_size=482 inflight=98
```

Marco Diaz: Is autoscaler not replenishing warm nodes? We had a maintenance window earlier that drained a subset of warm pool.

Infra Oncall: Exactly — warm-pool glidepath job failed during maintenance due to a cert expiration. Autoscaler didn't create replacement instances fast enough; admission control hit hard caps.

Katie Nguyen: Quick mitigation options: 1) Temporarily enlarge commitment-az1 quota (fast but impacts cost), 2) Throttle noisy tenants via fairshare, 3) Enable fallback to quantized model variant for some routes.

Sanjay Rao: Do 2 + 3 now. Approve a short quota bump only if we can't stabilize in 10m.

Infra Oncall: Applying fairshare delta to reduce noisy tenant weight and enabling fallback for the busiest route. Commands run: 
```bash
# lower weight for tenant 238
redwoodctl fairshare update --pool commitment-az1 --tenant org-238 --weight 0.6
# flip fallback to quantized model for route /v1/generate
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --fallback-model rw-q8b --enable-fallback true
```

Lena Park: After the changes queue_size dropped from 482 -> 130 over ~4m, p95 latency improving. We'll keep monitoring.

Aisha Patel: Noting customer impact and comms. I can draft a short heartbeat to affected Dedicated customers once we confirm stability.

Marco Diaz: Cost note — fallback to q8b reduces cost per token but may affect quality. Product aware?

Sanjay Rao: Product (Aisha / Marco) — we ship the fallback only to non-SLA routes for now. Keep SLA customers on main model; if we need quota bump, inform sales.

Infra Oncall: Warming one additional GPU node in ap-sg-1 while glidepath job is being fixed. Temp scale command: `kubectl scale deploy/warm-pool-ap-sg-1 --replicas=3` (was 2 -> 3). Also restarted glidepath job and rotated cert referenced in job config.

ops-bot: Autoscaler job restart recorded (job-run-6743).

Katie Nguyen: Reconfigured admission soft-limit from 0.85 -> 0.8 to reduce head-of-line blocking and give room for warm nodes to come online.

Lena Park: Metrics now stabilizing. p95 token latency trending down to 1.1s, queue_size ~48. No new 429 spike in last 3m.

Aisha Patel: Drafted status note to customers and included ETA for full remediation (2h). Link: https://redwood.status/incidents/INC-2026-442-dedicated-ap-sg

Sanjay Rao: Followups: (1) Postmortem to cover glidepath cert expiry and hardening (owner: Aisha), (2) Autoscaler fallback tests to verify warm pool rebuild race (owner: Marco), (3) Consider adding burst quota runway to avoid immediate hard caps (owner: Katie).

Infra Oncall: Will keep oncall until stable. If we don't get to steady-state in 30m, escalate to SRE lead for emergency quota.

Marco Diaz: Created follow-up tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2310 (glidepath cert rotation), https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2311 (warm-pool stress test).

Sanjay Rao: Thanks team. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now — continue monitoring and update INC-2026-442 with timeline and postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident updated INC-2026-442 status=mitigated assignees=[Infra Oncall, Aisha Patel, Marco Diaz]
